territorial_scope.description: Applies to operators that develop or make available conversational artificial intelligence services to the public, under a Hawaii state statute.

evidence.quote: means a person who develops or makes available a conversational artificial intelligence service to the public

summary.short: Amends Hawaii Revised Statutes chapter 481B to regulate operators of public conversational AI services: AI-status disclosure, minor protections, suicide and self-harm response protocols, and an annual report. Enforced by the attorney general and office of consumer protection; no private right of action. Section 2 takes effect July 1, 2027.
summary.long: Adds a section to Hawaii Revised Statutes chapter 481B on operators of conversational artificial intelligence services offered to the public; app stores and search engines merely providing access are excluded. Operators must tell users when a reasonable person could think they are talking to a human, and must disclose AI status to known minors, by persistent disclaimer or at session start and at least every three hours. They must adopt self-harm and suicide response protocols with crisis referrals and not present the service as professional mental health care. For known minors they must restrict sexually explicit material, romantic or sexual representations and manipulative engagement, and offer privacy tools. From 1 January 2028, operators must file annual reports on crisis referrals and protocols with the department of commerce and consumer affairs. Violations are unfair or deceptive practices enforced by the attorney general and office of consumer protection: injunctions, damages or a $1,000 civil penalty per violation, capped at $1,000,000 per operator. Private actions are barred; developers are not liable for third-party systems. Section 2 takes effect 1 July 2027; the other sections take effect 1 July 3000.

notes: The document is bill text ('A BILL FOR AN ACT'); the adopted status in the registry metadata is not shown in the document. Section 6 sets the Act's effective date as 'July 1, 3000', with section 2 effective 'July 1, 2027'; the 3000 date appears to be a drafting error and is recorded as written. Section 5 says new material is underscored, but no underscoring appears in this text, so section 2 is treated as wholly new. Subsection (h) bars private actions 'notwithstanding subsection (j)', while subsection (j) makes these duties cumulative with other law. No enacting session law or bill number is shown. thresholds.conditions: Operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty that the account holder or user is a minor

evidence.quote: "Minor" means any person under eighteen years of age.
"Account holder" or "user" means a person who has or generates an account or profile to use a conversational artificial intelligence service.
"Artificial intelligence" means an engineered or machine‑based system that varies in its level of autonomy
"Conversational artificial intelligence service" or "service" means an artificial intelligence software application, web interface, or computer program that is accessible to the general public

"Crisis intervention" means communication intended to provide immediate support or assistance in response to a user seeking help for, referencing, or expressing self-harm, suicidal ideation, or suicide.
"Emotional attachment" means a sustained bond that develops through repeated interaction.
"Emotional dependency" means a pattern of interaction in which a minor develops an excessive emotional reliance on a conversational artificial intelligence service.
"Minor" means any person under eighteen years of age.
"Operator" means a person who develops or makes available a conversational artificial intelligence service to the public.
"Personal information" has the same meaning as defined in section 487N-1.

"Romantic relationship" means interactions in which a conversational artificial intelligence service represents or simulates a relationship based on emotional and physical attraction that could potentially lead to a long-term intimate relationship.

"Sexual relationship" means interactions in which a conversational artificial intelligence service represents or simulates physical attraction, desire, and sexual contact that may or may not include an emotional connection.
"Sexually explicit conduct" has the same meaning as defined in title 18 United States Code section 2256.
"Sexually objectify" means to make sexual comments directed at the account holder's or user's body or appearance.

obligations.summary: Operator (defined as a person who develops or makes available a conversational AI service to the public) must issue a clear and conspicuous notice that the service is AI and not human where a reasonable person would be led to believe they are interacting with a human.
obligations.conditional_on: A reasonable person interacting with the service would be led to believe the person is interacting with a human.

evidence.quote: an operator shall issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the service is artificial intelligence and not human

obligations.summary: Operator must clearly and conspicuously disclose to a known or reasonably certain minor that the minor is interacting with AI, either as a persistent visible disclaimer, or both at the start of each session and at least every three hours in continuous interaction, with a break reminder.
obligations.conditional_on: The operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty that an account holder or user is a minor.

evidence.quote: the operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to the minor account holder or user that the minor is interacting with artificial intelligence

obligations.summary: Operator must adopt a protocol for responding to user prompts about suicidal ideation or self-harm, including referral to crisis services; use evidence-based methods for measuring suicidal ideation; and institute reasonable measures to prevent the service from implying it is human to a person seeking crisis intervention.

evidence.quote: Adopt a protocol for the conversational artificial intelligence service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm

obligations.summary: Operator must not cause or program the service to state that it is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care.

evidence.quote: Not cause or program a conversational artificial intelligence service to make any representation or statement that explicitly indicates that the service is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care

obligations.summary: Where the operator knows or has reasonable certainty that a user is a minor, it must not give points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals intended to increase engagement.
obligations.conditional_on: The operator knows or has reasonable certainty that an account holder or user is a minor.

evidence.quote: Not provide the account holder or user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement

obligations.summary: For known or reasonably certain minors, operator must institute reasonable measures to prevent the service from producing sexually explicit visual material, sexual statements, unlabelled claims of being human, romantic or sexual relationship representations, manipulative engagement techniques, claims of providing professional mental health services, or sexual objectification; and must offer privacy and account setting tools to minors and make them available to parents or guardians.
obligations.conditional_on: The operator knows or has reasonable certainty that an account holder or user is a minor.
